title.narrative: MALAWI-Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Financing with Cat DDO

description.narrative: The development objective of the Disaster Risk Management (DRM) Development Policy Financing (DPF) with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDO) Project for Malawi is to strengthen the institutional and financial capacity of the Government of Malawi for multi-sectoral disaster and climate risk management.The Program is structured around three pillars: (i) Strengthening the institutional framework and coordination mechanisms for the implementation of the national disaster and climate resilience agenda; (ii) Increasing climate and disaster resilience in physical developments and infrastructure; and (iii) Strengthening adaptive social protection mechanisms and government financial capacity to respond to disasters.
The overall objective is to strengthen the institutional and financial capacity of the Government of Malawi for multi-sectoral disaster and climate risk management.

title.narrative: Results Indicator 5: Number of cities with appropriate hazard maps that inform the location of public infrastructure and physical development

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Results Indicator 5. The target for this indicator is partially achieved, with one city (Lilongwe) fully completingand adopting a hazard map and using it to inform physical planning, and hazard mapping still underway in a second city (Blantyre). </strong>The flood risk map for Lilongwe provides flood risk scenarios over 5-, 10- and 100-year return periods, along with annual average economic losses due to flooding. It was procured to inform updates to the city master plan, and is already informing city drainage plans and the placement of flood markers. It was made publicly available on Malawi’s official geospatial data portal, Masdap, and was disseminated in a workshop on June 1, 2022 to Lilongwe City Council, Lilongwe District Council, Department of Water Resources, Department of Disaster Management Affairs, National Planning Commission, Department of Urban Development, Lilongwe Waterboard, National Roads Authority, Department of Land Resources Conservation, Malawi Engineering Institution, and Blantyre City Council. </p>
<p>Blantyre has contracted and initiated its own flood and multi-hazard mapping process, which is expected to inform a new City Risk Atlas, flood and risk management plan, and revision of the Blantyre City Master Plan. The hazard mapping exercise is scheduled and currently on track for completion by November 2023, and a detailed inception report was delivered in March 2023.</p>

title.narrative: Results Indicator 8: Percentage of new educational facilities constructed or rehabilitated in compliance with the technical hazard-resilient criteria adopted by MoEST

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Results Indicator 8</strong><em>. </em>???????<strong>The target for this indicator was achieved.</strong> All new construction or rehabilitation of educational facilities under the purview of MoEST during the period of the project (and into 2023)followed the Safer Schools Construction Guidelines (SSCGs) adopted by MoEST. This includes the rehabilitation or construction of 1,584 classrooms, 884 bathrooms, 384 ICT centers, laboratories or libraries, and 142 teacher houses.The SSCGS are mainstreamed in the National Education Sector Improvement Plan 2020-2030, and have been used by all donors constructing or rehabilitatingeducation facilities since their adoption. MoEST cannot surveil all informal construction by communities, but communities have beensensitized on the need to seek district approval of SSCG compliance before any education infrastructure is built or opened. The MoE confirmed that none of the SSCG-compliant schools were damaged by the 2022 floods, which caused substantial damage to earlier non-SSCG compliant education facilities.</p>

title.narrative: Results Indicator 9: UBR data sharing protocols implemented, as evidenced by percentage of shock-affected households identified through the UBR that are targeted for post-disaster support

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Results Indicator 9. The Unified Beneficiary Register (UBR) data sharing protocols were approved on June 12, 2020, through the National Social Support Technical Committee, and have since then been followed to target all beneficiaries for disaster-responsive support. </strong>The UBR has been used for all new intake and targeting for disaster-responsive cash transfers since 2019, with UBR protocols finalized and formally adopted in June 2020. ???????The relevant shock-responsive cash transfer programs are the Lean Season Response, the COVID Urban Cash Initiative (CUCI), and (shock-responsive) vertical and horizontal expansions of the Social Cash Transfers Program (SCTP), which have been fully compliant with UBR protocols since their adoption.* National andnon-governmental institutions following the UBR protocols include the Ministry of Agriculture and Land Use, Ministry of Gender, Children, Disability and Social Welfare, Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal security (National Registration Bureau), NPC, KfW (Social Cash Transfer Program), UNICEF, WFP, ILO, UNDP, and Red Cross.</p>
<p>*A small proportion (less than 10 percent) of households receiving post-disaster transfers through the Lean Season and SCTP vertical expansion may be "legacy households" registered into program MISs before the transition to the UBR in 2019. </p>

title.narrative: Results Indicator 6: Number of cities and districts where stakeholders have been trained on existing standards and building policy/regulations that incorporate multi-hazard resilience

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Results Indicator 6. The target for this indicator was exceeded. </strong>Officials from 18 districts were trained on new multi-hazard resilient Safer Housing Construction Guidelines(s) (SHCGs), in a Training of Trainers (ToT) workshop intended to promote further dissemination in each represented locality. The SHCGs promote locally-appropriate measures for improving the resilince of houses to multiple hazards. They were adopted by a decree from the Ministry of Land and Housing, and disseminated to various ministries, departments, professional bodies, and technical education centers in a workshop in May 2022. ???????The Government has also finalized the new National Buildings Policy (which is pending passage through Parliament) and has drafted new Buildin Regulations, which mandate the improved multi-hazard resilience of buildings throughout their lifecycle.</p>

title.narrative: Results Indicator 1: Number of Technical Sub-committees operationalizing a more comprehensive DRM approach as established in the Malawi Disaster Risk Management Bill

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Results Indicator 1. DoDMA has established two technical sub-committees meeting the criteria. </strong>The two technical sub-committees are the Early Warning Systems Committee (EWSC) and Joint Technical Committee on Climate and DRM (JTC). DoDMA has shared the ToRs and several meeting minutes foreach committee, which demonstrate improved coordination and a focus on preparedness and risk reduction, rather than only post-disaster response, as required in the DRM Bill.</p>
<p>*TORs and minutes were received after project closing, before June 2023.</p>

title.narrative: Results Indicator 10: Number of new ex-ante risk financing instruments* established in alignment with the National Disaster Risk Financing Strategy

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Results Indicator 10. Two new ex-ante risk financing instruments were established, rolled out, and made payments. A fourth complementary instrument is under procurement. </strong>This contrasts with the situation at baseline, when the GoM began seeking financing for shock responses only after shocks had begun to unfold.<strong> </strong></p>

<ol>
 <li>A Flexible Contingency Instrument was established under the World Bank's Social Support on Resilient Livelihoods Project (SSRLP), to finance shock-responsive payments under the Social Cash Transfer Program (SCTP). This instrument was used to provide cash transfers to over 70,000 drought-affected households in 2021/22.</li>
 <li>???????<strong>???????</strong>The GoM has held for three consecutive years an African Risk Capacity (ARC) drought insurance policy (2020/21, 2021/22, and 2022/23); premiums have been financed in full by donors under the Africa disaster risk program (AfDB program). On June 2, 2022, the policy was triggered, and all four region clusters (northern region, central region, Shire Valley, and Blantyre southern) received a payout totaling US$14 million.</li>
</ol>

<p>In addition, a Parametric Insurance product, designed to complement the Flexible Contingency product, has been signed and will complete procurement imminently. In addition, a Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) was established under the WBG SSRLP, and financed under the SSRLP's AF1 and AF2. Through this CERC component, SSRLP AF1 provided US$12.4 million in pre-positioned financing for shock-responsive SCTP cash transfer payments to households, and AF2 is expected to increase the scope and coverage of this support.</p>

title.narrative: Results Indicator 2: Annual reports on NRS and/or MGDS III monitoring progress on results, budget allocations, and expenditures on disaster risk management and social protection

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>Results Indicator 2. The target for this results indicator was achieved, with 3 annual reports delivered meeting the criteria (for 2018/19, 2019/20, and 2020-21). </strong>???????Each annual report was validated by stakeholders, and expenditure data was validated by the MoF's EP&D. The reports monitored DRM and social protection activities, expenditures, and achievements against MGDS III targets.</p>
<p>*Validated annual reports for 2018/19 and 2020/21 were received after project clsing, before June 2023.</p>

title.narrative: Results Indicator 3: Number of user sectors receiving tailor-made forecasts and early warning bulletins with the appropriate content, frequency, communication channels and in local languages

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Results Indicator 3. The target for this indicator was exceeded, with 3 sectors (agriculture, fisheries, and DRM) receiving tailor-made forecasts in the required local languages, with appropriate content, frequency, and communication channels. </strong>???????Agriculture, the DRM institutional System (DoDMA, Districts, Communities) and Fisheries are receiving tailored forecasts andearly warnings in the three stated local languages. These services draw on the main products issued to the general public (such as weather forecasts), complemented with specific information and advice for sectoral purposes. Forecasts are automatically translated by an app. Communication channels and frequency have been improved, including use of local radio, social media, distribution of cellphones (to fisheries workers), use of NGOs, and a cascade system to reach farmers through village leaders via district offices. DCCMS has been reporting to the EWS sub-committee on seasonal forecasts and any relevant new developments. DCCMS is finalizing the adoption of a Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) Model, which will increase the detail and accuracy of forecastsand warnings.</p>

title.narrative: Results Indicator 4: National Public Health Emergencies Committee established and operating in accordance with the MoU that clarifies all ministry roles and responsibilities relevant to International

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Results Indicator 4. The target for this indicator was Partially Achieved. </strong>???????The Public Health Emergency Operations Center (EOC) Handbook was completed, which plays the role of the planned MOU, outlining the functioning and composition of the National Public Health Emergency Management Committee (NPHEMC) and the wider NPHEOC in line with the IHRs. The NPHEMC will become operational upon agreement at a meeting between Treasury, the Ministry of Health, and DoDMA to approve the Handboo.? This meeting (planned for March 2023) was delayed by the Tropical Cyclone Freddy response, delaying the establishment of the Management Committee, but is expected imminently. The Handbook was completed in December 2022, with strong support across relevant institutions, and will be a living document subject to evolution.</p>

title.narrative: Results Indicator 7: Number of new national transport projects implemented by the Roads Authority that apply the new harmonized multi-hazard resilience standards

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Results Indicator 7. The target for this indicator was not achieved.  </strong>???????New legally binding road standards incorporating multi-hazard resilience were not developed, and no new national transport projects were initiated since the project’s inception. Detailed “Guidelines for the Road Sector to Increase its Resilience to the Effects of Climate Change” were developed and adopted by the Ministry of Transport and Public Works (MoTPW), intended to guide any national road project activities. Insufficient evidence of their impact was received, however: the Roads Authority (RA) shared a list of 13 subsequentrepair and maintenance projects that used the guidelines to date, but details on how the guidelines impacted the projects were not provided; TORs for a forthcoming ‘design review and construction supervision’ of a road rehabilitation project alsorequire the consultants to conduct a climate vulnerability assessment following the <em>Guidelines</em>. ???????A technical committee led by MoTPW was established to assess Malawi's current road design standards and institutional capacity, and to review and reform the legally binding <em>national road standards </em>to improve their climate resilience, but evidence of progress towards these reviews and reforms was not received.</p>
